beats.caption: The first hashtag anyone proposed on Twitter.

beats.name: Chris Messina
beats.role: a product consultant, posted the idea to Twitter on 23 August, asking how people felt about using the pound sign for groups.

beats.lead: He was not inventing the symbol.
beats.text: Internet Relay Chat had used the pound sign to label channels since around 1988.
beats.note: Messina adapted an existing convention rather than starting from nothing.

beats.text: Twitter did not adopt the idea. Its own users did, that October, tagging posts about the San Diego wildfires so people could follow the story.
beats.note: Twitter itself only began turning hashtags into clickable links on 2 July 2009, almost two years after the original tweet.

beats.text: Messina never tried to patent it. He said hashtags were born of the internet, and owned by no one.

beats.line: A punctuation mark that took over the internet.
